text:
alex: Heads-up — saw duplicated prefetches thrashing the shared cache on a 3-node pool this morning, p95 latency spikes during warmup.

maria: ugh. any quick repro or logs?

alex: attaching snippets in thread but gist: multiple requests for overlapping safetensors shards triggered independent prefetch tasks, eviction chasing. pattern: concurrent canary + rollover traffic. :grimacing:

devon: is the dedupe key currently just the shard id? or does it include byte-range and quantization variant?

alex: right now it's shard_id only. that was intentional to be simple, but it means different byte-range warmups collide.

sam: think we should switch to a compound key: (model_version, shard_id, byte_range_hash, quant_profile). cheap to compute. avoids duplicate IO.

ira: two related tradeoffs: 1) larger dedupe key reduces duplicate IO but may prevent legitimate parallelism when different ranges are actually needed concurrently; 2) compound keys increase memory for in-flight map.

maria: also need admission control: if warmup queue > X, demote prefetch to background low-priority and let request miss and stream instead. otherwise we keep destabilizing cache.

alex: agreed. proposal sketch: 1) dedupe key = model+shard+range_hash+quant_id, 2) admission watermark at per-GPU and cluster-wide levels, 3) soft-priority lanes (canary/latency-sensitive vs background), 4) fallback to mmap-read-on-demand for small ranges.

devon: small nit — for safetensors the manifest gives contiguous slices; for packed formats we need range normalization. implement canonical byte-range canonicalizer to avoid equivalent keys differing.

sam: +1. also add a short TTL on in-flight entries: if a prefetch hasn't completed in Y ms assume it failed and allow a repeated attempt with backoff. prevents stuck locks.

ira: what about atomicity and partial writes? if prefetch writes a partially filled cache entry and eviction reads it, we need either a write-temp-then-rename or a presence flag. small state machine: INIT -> WRITING -> READY -> EVICTED.

alex: exactly. propose using a tiny header in cache object with state and checksum. readers must check READY before using. makes eviction easier.

maria: we should also emit metrics: dedupe_hits, dedupe_misses, prefetch_time_ms, prefetch_failures, in_flight_count, starvation_events. dashboards for the next week.

warmup-bot: deploy queued: warmup-controller v1.3.2 (prefetch dedupe) scheduled to staging at 09:10 UTC.

devon: regressions to watch: latency for first-request cold paths, memory footprint of in-flight map, corner-case when quant_profile is missing (defaulting key may hide variant mismatch).

sam: for missing quant_profile — include model manifest version as tie-breaker, and when unknown, use the conservative path: no dedupe across unknown-quant.

ira: long-term thought: unify per-GPU shared cache with a lightweight distributed index so warmup for hot shards can coordinate across nodes (avoid redundant copies). bigger project though.

alex: yeah that is the post-optimization. for now we want low-risk changes: canonicalize ranges, compound key, TTL+backoff, write-state header, and admission watermarks. I'll open a small RFC PR with the code sketch and perf microbench plan.

maria: please include test harness: synthetic concurrent warmup with safetensors manifests + packed-tar fallback. run on staging pool and capture dedupe metrics.

alex: will do. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
